of-gerar-yaml.enunciado: Create the api Deployment (image kubelearn/loja:1.0, 3 replicas) without writing the YAML from scratch: generate it with kubectl, save it to api.yaml and apply it.
of-gerar-yaml.dica: kubectl create deployment api --image=kubelearn/loja:1.0 --replicas=3 --dry-run=client -o yaml > api.yaml && kubectl apply -f api.yaml (here, one command at a time)
of-gerar-yaml.vidaReal: Asking the builder for the standard blueprint already filled in, instead of drawing every wall by hand.
of-gerar-yaml.limite: The generated blueprint has the basics: probes, resources and the rest you still add to the file.

testes.descricao: the api was generated, saved and applied

msgs.0: you generated the YAML with --dry-run=client -o yaml > api.yaml

of-expor.titulo: A phone extension in one command
of-expor.enunciado: Give the loja (store) a NodePort Service on port 80, delivering to the pods’ 8080, with a single command.
of-expor.vidaReal: Asking for the phone extension over the phone, without filling in a form.
of-expor.limite: expose copies the Deployment’s selector at that moment: if the labels change later, the Service doesn’t follow.

of-trocar-versao.enunciado: Switch the loja image to kubelearn/loja:1.1 from the terminal and watch the rollout until it finishes.
of-trocar-versao.dica: kubectl set image deployment/loja loja=kubelearn/loja:1.1 and then kubectl rollout status deployment/loja
of-trocar-versao.vidaReal: Replacing the clerk at one counter at a time, without closing the store, and watching until the last one is swapped.
of-trocar-versao.limite: set image changes the cluster, not your file: the next apply of the old YAML brings the old version back.

testes.descricao: the store is on 1.1, and you watched it

msgs.1: you watched it with rollout status

of-desfazer.enunciado: Someone shipped a loja version that crashes as soon as it starts. Go back to the previous version with one command.
of-desfazer.vidaReal: Undoing the renovation that went wrong: the old painting goes back on the wall.
of-desfazer.limite: undo rolls back the Deployment, not the database: whatever the broken version wrote stays written.

of-rotulos.enunciado: Put the label tier=frontend on every vitrine (storefront) pod (all at once, by selector) and list only the pods with that label.
of-rotulos.dica: kubectl label pods -l app=vitrine tier=frontend and then kubectl get pods -l tier=frontend
of-rotulos.vidaReal: Putting the same sticker on every door of a floor and then calling only the ones with the sticker.
of-rotulos.limite: The label goes on today’s pods: a new pod from the Deployment is born without it (to last, the label goes in the template).

msgs.0: you labeled them by selector (-l app=vitrine)

of-jsonpath.enunciado: Which image does the cofre (safe) Deployment use? Find out with -o jsonpath (only the image in the output) and answer below.
of-jsonpath.vidaReal: Asking the doorman for just the apartment number, not the resident’s whole file.
of-jsonpath.limite: jsonpath picks the exact field: if the list has two containers, [0] shows only the first.

testes.descricao: you found the image with jsonpath

of-autoscale.enunciado: Create an HPA for the loja from 2 to 6 replicas, targeting 60% CPU, with a single command.
of-autoscale.vidaReal: Hiring the temp-staff manager with all the rules at once: minimum, maximum and when to call in help.
of-autoscale.limite: The command creates the HPA, but without CPU requests on the pods it can’t compute the percentage.

of-colunas.enunciado: Build a table of the Deployments with only two columns, NOME and IMAGEM, using -o custom-columns. Which Deployment uses the nginx:1.28 image?
of-colunas.vidaReal: Asking the management office for a spreadsheet with just each resident’s name and phone number, not the whole file.
of-colunas.limite: Each column is a fixed path: if a Deployment has two containers, [0] shows only the first one’s image.

testes.descricao: you built the table and found the Deployment

of-ordenar.enunciado: List the pods in creation order, with --sort-by (the newest ends up at the bottom). Which Deployment do the newest pods belong to?
of-ordenar.vidaReal: Asking for the list of residents in order of arrival, to find who moved in yesterday.
of-ordenar.limite: The order follows the field you pick: two pods created in the same second can show up in either order.

testes.descricao: you sorted and found the newest pods

of-eventos.enunciado: Some Deployment in the neighborhood isn’t coming up. Without opening pod after pod, list only the namespace’s warnings with kubectl events --types=Warning. Which Deployment has the problem?
of-eventos.dica: kubectl events --types=Warning (the OBJECT column says who the warning is about)
of-eventos.vidaReal: Reading only the complaints in the front desk log, not the whole log.
of-eventos.limite: Events disappear after an hour: an old problem with no new warning won’t show up here anymore.

testes.descricao: you filtered the warnings and found the problem

of-patch.enunciado: On the next version rollout, loja can’t take any pod down before its replacement is ready: set maxUnavailable: 0 in its strategy with kubectl patch, without opening a file.
of-patch.vidaReal: Replacing one roof tile without redoing the whole roof.
of-patch.limite: The patch changes the cluster, not your file: on the next apply of the old YAML, the field goes back to what it says there.

testes.descricao: loja rolls out without taking anyone down

of-set-env.enunciado: Add the environment variable MODO=manutencao to loja with kubectl set env.
of-set-env.vidaReal: Changing the notice on the front desk board without reprinting the house rules.
of-set-env.limite: Changing env changes the template: the Deployment replaces every pod, one by one, as if it were a new version.
